synTagma[^syntagma] is a spatial coordinate space computing system based on [Tagma](/projects/syntagma/tagma/), where the address is the coordinate — not a flat pointer, but a point in an N-dimensional geometric space. This is made possible by a 16-bit Unicode block allocated to a 3-axis writing system, which provides a collision-free, hash-less, structurally addressable coordinate space. Every valid 16-bit value in this space is simultaneously a 1-D address (Unicode code point), a 3-D coordinate (initial, medial, final), and a displayable Hangul syllable. This triple interpretation enables hash-less content addressing with zero collision probability and single-cycle combinational decoding at an estimated ~300 gates[^spec-status]. Every content-addressable system today generates identifiers through a hash function. SHA-256. UUID. Hash tables. The industry's answer to this cost has been faster hash units and larger hash tables -- never questioning whether hashing is needed at all. The Tagma primitive shows it is not: the identifier is not a random-looking hex string but a pronounceable syllable carrying its own coordinate system.

Unicode assigns each script a fixed address block. Within this block, Hangul occupies a contiguous 16-bit segment (U+AC00--U+D7AF) invented in 1443 and allocated in Unicode 2.0 in 1996. Its composition formula embeds three independent structural axes into every code point:

$$C(i,m,f) = \text{U+AC00} + 588i + 28m + f$$
$$\quad (0 \leq i < 19,\; 0 \leq m < 21,\; 0 \leq f < 28)$$

A hardware decoder extracts the three axis fields in one cycle. Of 65,536 possible 16-bit values, 11,172 are structurally valid and the remaining 54,364 are immediately detectable as invalid. CoordPath chains multiple syllables into higher dimensions (6 = 18 axes, 19 = 57 axes), with each axis position representing a different application-defined dimension -- region, device type, timestamp, shard. The arithmetic operations are invariant; only the axis interpretation changes per deployment.

No other Unicode script satisfies all four conditions required: a contiguous fixed-width 16-bit address range, a closed-form composition formula, a complete three-axis decomposition, and an open international standard. Hangul is unique.

```{python}
#| include: false
import numpy as np

n_init, n_med, n_fin = 19, 21, 28
stride = 2
init_vals = np.arange(0, n_init, stride)
med_vals  = np.arange(0, n_med,  stride)
fin_vals  = np.arange(0, n_fin,  stride)

I, M, F = np.meshgrid(init_vals, med_vals, fin_vals, indexing='ij')
I_f, M_f, F_f = [a.flatten() for a in (I, M, F)]

def box_edges(x0, y0, z0, x1, y1, z1):
    edges = []
    def add(xa, ya, za, xb, yb, zb):
        edges.append(((xa, ya, za), (xb, yb, zb)))
    for (dx, dy, dz) in [(x1,y0,z0),(x0,y1,z0),(x0,y0,z1)]:
        add(x0,y0,z0,dx,dy,dz)
    add(x1,y1,z0, x1,y0,z0); add(x1,y1,z0, x0,y1,z0); add(x1,y1,z0, x1,y1,z1)
    add(x0,y1,z1, x1,y1,z1); add(x0,y1,z1, x0,y0,z1); add(x0,y1,z1, x0,y1,z0)
    add(x1,y0,z1, x1,y1,z1); add(x1,y0,z1, x1,y0,z0); add(x1,y0,z1, x0,y0,z1)
    return edges

full_edges  = box_edges(0, 0, 0, 31, 31, 31)
valid_edges = box_edges(0, 0, 0, 18, 20, 27)
```

## The cost of hashing: what Tagma removes

Every hash-based identity system consumes energy and area before producing a single useful result. A SHA-256 engine requires approximately 10,000 gates and 64-75 cycles per operation, then needs a hash table, collision resolution, and dynamic resizing. UUID generation requires entropy collection and still delivers probabilistic uniqueness with 128-bit identifiers expressed as 36 hex characters.

The Tagma decoder replaces all of this with a combinational decoder and a 16-bit register. The output is not an opaque hex string but a readable Hangul syllable -- or a sequence of syllables for larger spaces. A single syllable covers 11,172 identifiers. Six syllables (18 axes) cover $1.9 \times 10^{24}$ identifiers, exceeding typical distributed system needs. Nineteen syllables match the full SHA-256 space of $2^{256}$. At every scale, the identifier is human-readable, self-validating, and free of special characters.

Measured software cost on Apple M1: 2 ns per single-syllable identifier vs 227 ns for SHA-256 (115x faster). At SHA-256 scale (19 syllables): 35 ns vs 227 ns (6.5x faster). For spatial queries, CoordSpace outperforms HashMap by 2.3--2.4x on axis and range filters, and CoordSet compound queries achieve 129x throughput over HashMap scan -- because the coordinate space eliminates indirection at every level.

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

## Verification by exhaustive enumeration

The Tagma coordinate space is exhaustively enumerable: 65,536 possible 16-bit values, of which exactly 11,172 satisfy the composition formula. A verification harness generates all 65,536 inputs, applies the decoder specification, and records every result. The bijection is verified by enumeration: no collisions, no unassigned values within the block. Every implementation, hardware or software, can be verified against the same ground truth in milliseconds on any commodity system.

This is not possible with hash-based systems. A SHA-256 engine cannot be exhaustively verified across its full input space. The Tagma coordinate space can, because it is bounded and its formula is closed-form.

## Application domains

**Embedded and sensor systems.** The 11,172-identifier space fits entirely in a single no-allocator array of 22 KB (89 KB for 64-bit values). Every Coord is a direct array index: one load, no hashing, no collisions, no resizing. A zero-initialized array gives bulk operations a 15x advantage over HashMap for this class of use.

**LLM inference cache.** Key-value caches indexed by token sequence prefixes currently use hash tables or radix trees. synTagma replaces this with CoordPath-based direct access: each prefix maps to a unique CoordPath, lookup cost is O(1) direct array accesses with zero hash computation. Production cache sizes (typically $10^4$--$10^7$ entries) are covered by 2--4 syllables.

**Graph and multi-dimensional query.** Each node maps to a Coord, each edge type to a CoordSet. Adjacency reduces to a bitwise AND over 175 machine words.

**Vector database and multi-dimensional indexing.** Tagma is not a faster vector DB -- it is a different layer entirely. Where vector DBs index embedding similarity through approximate search with recall trade-offs, Tagma resolves axis-projection and set-membership queries through direct coordinate arithmetic. This is a new infrastructure layer where address, identity, and geometry converge into a single structure. Applications that fit the coordinate model -- structured multi-attribute keys, axis-aligned filtering, set-based compound conditions -- bypass the index layer entirely rather than optimizing it.

**General-purpose content addressing.** Wherever UUIDs, hash keys, or sequence-number identifiers are used today -- database records, distributed nodes, file identifiers, commit hashes -- synTagma provides a shorter, faster, human-readable alternative with zero collision probability.

## Boundaries

Tagma does not replace cryptographic primitives. SHA-256 remains for signatures, Merkle proofs, and preimage resistance. Encryption, authentication, and key derivation are outside the primitive's scope. Tagma replaces the use of hashes as structural identifiers and addresses. The two can also be combined: SHA-256 output encoded as 19 Hangul syllables is more readable than 64 hex characters while preserving the same $2^{-256}$ collision probability.

synTagma is built on open international standards and runs on open ISA (RISC-V) -- unencumbered by proprietary licensing or regional dependencies. The Tagma primitive is a neutral, sovereign coordinate space for the global computing landscape.

## 588년 전의 설계, 데이터 주소 체계가 되다

1443년 창제된 한글은 초성 19, 중성 21, 종성 28이라는 세 독립 축의 조합으로 음절을 구성합니다. 이 완성형 음절은 예외 규칙이 없으며, 유니코드 표준(U+AC00–U+D7AF)에서 16비트 고정 공간에 연속적으로 배정되어 있습니다. 동시에 초성·중성·종성의 조합 원리는 그대로 3차원 좌표 표현이 됩니다. 더욱이 이 공간은 유니코드 기본 정의 공간(BMP, Plane 0)에 속해 있어, 모든 컴퓨팅 인프라 계층에서 별도 설정 없이도 오류 없이 다뤄지며 인간이 식별 가능한 음절로 해석됩니다. 이는 아파트 동-호수 체계와 쉽게 비유할 수 있으며, 건물의 층수와 호실 배열이 일관되게 정의되어 있다면, "101호"라는 주소만으로 중앙 안내판(해시 테이블) 없이 즉시 해당 방의 위치를 알 수 있습니다. Tagma는 한글 음절 좌표를 이와 같은 원리로, 모든 컴퓨팅 인프라와 컴파일러가 공통으로 사용하는 국제 유니코드 표준을 주소 표준으로 활용하는 체계입니다.

Tagma는 이 네 가지 조건—(1) 16비트 고정 공간, (2) 완전한 조합 구조, (3) 코드 포인트에 반영된 3축 좌표, (4) 국제 표준(ISO/IEC 10646) 공공재—이 모두 겹치는 덕분에 성립하는 수학적 기반위에 해시 함수 없이도 충돌 없는 무한한 식별자 공간을 생성하는 점을 이용해, 근본적인 데이터 처리 방식을 실제 다양한 소프트웨어와 하드웨어 계층의 구현을 통해 이를 모든 컴퓨팅 분야에 적용하는 프로젝트 입니다. 따라서 산술 연산만으로 데이터 주소를 추출하고 직접 접근하기 때문에 비교 불가능한 성능 향상을 달성하며, 좌표계의 기하학적 특성 덕분에 기존의 기하학적 공학 이론을 즉시 적용할 수 있습니다. 이는 기존의 암호화 체계를 대체하는 것이 아니라, 보완할 수 있는 계층으로 매우 단순한 원리 덕분에 기존의 암호화 알고리즘과 친화적인 연동성과 확장성이 보장됩니다.
